verdict.rationale: First-party docs say Fly.io runs apps as VMs in worldwide regions (18 regions), with explicit per-Machine region placement and users routed to the nearest server over a global Anycast network. Multi-region deployment is documented as a single command. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of latency gains near end users (the one community report of a performance uplift comes from a disclosed YC-connected founder), and no detail on edge-level footprint beyond 18 regions.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run my code on a global edge network close to end users

citations.quote: You can deploy apps in regions worldwide, so your users in Tokyo, São Paulo, or Amsterdam connect to the nearest server through our global Anycast network.
Fly Machines are hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second, run close to your users, and scale out to tens of thousands when the traffic arrives.
Run the APIs behind your product on VMs in 18 regions, close to your users.
You can create and destroy Machines directly, and you have control over every Machine’s lifecycle, resources, and region placement.
deploy to those regions with a single command
